t:
Paragraph (1) of section 502(c) of title 40, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) by striking “for automated” and inserting the following: “for the following:“(A) Automated”; and 
    (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(B) Alarm and signal systems, facility management systems, firefighting and rescue equipment, law enforcement and security equipment, marine craft and related equipment, special purpose clothing, and related services (as contained in Federal supply classification code group 84 or any amended or subsequent version of that Federal supply classification group).”.

fable.w: This section only amends 40 U.S.C. 502(c) to expand the categories of goods and services available under federal supply schedules. The tempting reading is that section 502(c) concerns state and local government use of federal supply schedules, so outside parties are involved. But buying from a schedule is not consulting, commenting on, or challenging a federal decision. The text creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, or right to sue.
fable.s: by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(B) Alarm and signal systems, facility management systems, firefighting and rescue equipment, law enforcement and security equipment, marine craft and related equipment, special purpose clothing, and related services

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to expand the list of items eligible for a specific procurement or supply classification. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The text is purely definitional and administrative regarding federal supply codes.
qwen_block.s: Paragraph (1) of section 502(c) of title 40, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “for automated” and inserting the following: “for the following:“(A) Automated”; and (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(B) Alarm and signal systems, facility management systems, firefighting and rescue equipment, law enforcement and security equipment, marine craft and related equipment, special purpose clothing, and related services (as contained in Federal supply classification code group 84 or any amended or subsequent version of that Federal supply classification group).”

opus.w: This amendment only adds a category of goods and services to an existing provision of 40 U.S.C. 502(c), which governs procurement through Federal supply schedules. One might read it as participation because that provision lets state and local governments use the schedules. But buying goods is procurement, akin to contracts or benefits, not consultation on a federal decision. The text has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
opus.s: (B) Alarm and signal systems, facility management systems, firefighting and rescue equipment, law enforcement and security equipment, marine craft and related equipment, special purpose clothing, and related services
opus.b:
I labelled this **No**. It is a technical amendment that adds a category of goods to an existing list, and it sets up no process for outside parties to take part in a federal decision.

- **Why it might look like a Yes:** 40 U.S.C. §502(c) is the provision that lets state and local governments buy from the GSA Federal Supply Schedules. That puts outside governments in the picture. (This comes from background knowledge of the statute, not from the amendment's own text.)
- **Why that fails:** State and local governments buying off a schedule are procuring goods. That is like an application for a contract or benefit, which the definition excludes. They are not being consulted on a federal decision.
- **What the text actually does:** It restructures the paragraph and adds a list of goods (alarm systems, firefighting equipment, security equipment and similar items in Federal supply classification group 84). It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the definition of items eligible for certain procurement methods. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a federal decision. There is no mention of public hearings, comment periods, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: Paragraph (1) of section 502(c) of title 40, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “for automated” and inserting the following: “for the following:“(A) Automated”; and (2) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(B) Alarm and signal systems, facility management systems, firefighting and rescue equipment, law enforcement and security equipment, marine craft and related equipment, special purpose clothing, and related services (as contained in Federal supply classification code group 84 or any amended or subsequent version of that Federal supply classification group).”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends a statute regarding procurement, it implicitly involves outside contractors. However, the text itself only defines categories of goods and services; it does not establish a process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. The definition requires an active mechanism for outside involvement (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board), which is absent here.
